title: U.S. House · California's 42nd District
area: Long Beach and surrounding Los Angeles County communities, redrawn under Proposition 50 (approved November 2025).

context.text: Incumbent Robert Garcia (D) and Republican Brian Burley advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, in which Garcia received 56.5% of the vote and Burley 20.6%, ahead of two other Republicans and a no-party-preference candidate.

candidates.name: Robert Garcia
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 56.5% of the vote.

summary.text: Robert Garcia is a Democrat who immigrated from Peru as a child, taught at Long Beach-area colleges and served on the Long Beach City Council (2009–2014) and as mayor of Long Beach (2014–2022). He was first elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and serves on the Oversight and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, where he became the Oversight Committee's ranking member in 2025. He is seeking re-election in the 42nd District.

background.text: Born in Lima, Peru, in 1977; according to Wikipedia he arrived in the United States with his mother in 1982 at age 5, graduated from Covina High School in 1995, and became a U.S. citizen in his early 20s.

Earned a bachelor's degree in communication studies from California State University, Long Beach (2002), a master's degree in communication management from the University of Southern California (2005), and an Ed.D. in higher education from CSU Long Beach (2010). Wikipedia notes he was Associated Students president at CSU Long Beach.
Worked as a professor of public policy and communications at USC, CSU Long Beach and Long Beach City College; Wikipedia also says he worked as a public information officer at Long Beach City College.
Founded the Long Beach Post, a local news and sports website, in 2007 and sold it before being elected mayor, according to Wikipedia.
Elected to the Long Beach City Council in 2009 and served until 2014, including as vice mayor from 2012 to 2014.
Elected mayor of Long Beach in a June 2014 runoff with 52% of the vote and re-elected in April 2018 with about 80%, serving until 2022, according to Wikipedia.
Won the 42nd District seat in November 2022, defeating Republican John Briscoe 68.4% to 31.6%, and took office January 3, 2023.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee, where he became ranking member on June 24, 2025, and on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee; Ballotpedia lists his earlier Homeland Security Committee assignment.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 56.5% of the vote to face Republican Brian Burley in the November general election.

priorities.text: Defending democracy, citing support for the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and the Freedom to Vote Act.
Raising the minimum wage and expanding the social safety net, including Medicaid, Social Security, Medicare and universal child care.
Expanding pathways to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

positions.summary: Says he will fight for a nationwide $15 minimum wage, citing his push to raise Long Beach's minimum wage to $15 an hour in 2016.
Says he supports Medicare for All and co-chairs Mayors 4 Medicare, and will fight to protect and expand Medicaid, Social Security and Medicare in Congress.
positions.quote: I believe the best approach to fixing our healthcare system is passing Medicare for All.

positions.summary: Says he strongly supports the Green New Deal and will fight to transition away from fossil fuels, citing Long Beach's fleet electrification and green-jobs programs under his mayoralty.

Says he will fight to expand pathways to citizenship for undocumented residents and end legal discrimination against them, citing his work establishing a legal defense fund and sanctuary-city protections in Long Beach.
Says every parent should be able to afford child care and that he will fight for universal child care and pre-K in Congress.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the Committee on Homeland Security, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure for the 2025-2026 term.

candidates.name: Brian Burley
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 20.6% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: Member, Huntington Beach City School District board (since 2024)

summary.text: Brian Burley is a Republican who owns an information-technology consulting and social-media marketing company in Huntington Beach and has worked as an IT analyst at the University of Southern California. He was elected to the Huntington Beach City School District board in 2024 after earlier unsuccessful runs for Huntington Beach City Council and for Congress in 2020 and 2022. According to his campaign website, he is running on tax relief, stronger immigration enforcement, support for law enforcement and the military, and family values.

background.text: Raised in a small town in Michigan, where his father was a forklift operator and his mother worked as a waitress and an accountant, according to his 2019 Candidate Connection survey.
Visited Huntington Beach in 2007 to see his mother, who had moved to California for cancer treatment; she died in 2011, and he says the experience shaped his interest in public service.

Attended California State University, Fullerton before transferring to the University of Southern California, where he earned a bachelor's degree in political economy and later a master's degree in public policy.
Owns an information-technology consulting and social-media marketing company based in Huntington Beach and has worked as an IT analyst at USC.

Ran for Huntington Beach City Council in 2018 and finished ninth of 15 candidates for four seats with 5.3% of the vote; ran as a Republican in the 2020 primary for California's 48th District (third, 12.1%), the 2022 primary for the 47th District (fourth, 7.1%), and withdrew from the 2024 primary for the 47th District.
Elected to the Huntington Beach City School District board in 2024; has been affiliated with the Orange County Central Committee of the California Republican Party.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary in the 42nd District with 20.6% of the vote, behind Robert Garcia.
According to his campaign website, he says his school-board service focused on parents' voices, student opportunity and stewardship of taxpayer dollars.

priorities.text: Says he will advocate for tax relief for families and business owners, take a stand against illegal immigration, fully support law enforcement and the military, and work to restore what he calls American family values.

Says his approach as a school board member — protecting parents' voices and stewarding taxpayer dollars responsibly — is the servant-leadership style he would bring to Congress, focused on safe neighborhoods, quality education and a strong economy.

positions.summary: Says he will take a stand against illegal immigration.
positions.quote: Take a Stand Against Illegal Immigration
